Little Abe tells the life of Abraham Lockwood, called the Bishop of Berry Brow. Berry Brow is a Yorkshire village of no pretensions to importance. Its only public building is a Mechanics' Institute of moderate size. One main street, substantially built, holds its life together. From these modest facts rises a local Methodist saint. F. Jewell wrote the life for the Methodist New Connexion. Small places made such bishops in that world.

Lockwood was a working preacher whose parish was one village. His monument is a life, not a building. Jewell's biography records sermons, conversions, and visitations in detail. It shows Wesleyan religion at its most local. Readers meet Victorian faith far below the famous pulpits. Little Abe's fame never left Yorkshire, which is the point.
